tool_args.content:
Depth Profiling: Classifying Recursive Generation Depth in Base-Model LLM Text

Our method has three stages:

(a) Recursive Generation Chain:
Human-written seed text (gen-0) is fed to a generator LLM G, producing gen-1 text. Gen-1 text is fed back to the same generator, producing gen-2 text, and so on: x^(k) = G(x^(k-1)). We use 8 base-model LLMs from 5 families (Pythia, OLMo, Qwen2.5, LLaMA-3.1, Mistral), ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters. The recursive chain produces texts at generation depths 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

(b) Feature Extraction and DDR Analysis:
Each text x^(k) is processed by a fixed reference model (Pythia-410M) to obtain per-token negative log-likelihood (NLL) distributions. From these distributions, we extract 5 NLL statistics: mean entropy (H_bar), entropy std (sigma_H), entropy min (H_min), entropy max (H_max), and tail decay (gamma). We also compute 2 surface-level features: type-token ratio (TTR) and hapax ratio. Total: 7 DDR (Differential Depth Response) features. The DDR framework reveals three response zones: DRIFTING features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) show monotonic shift with depth; INTERMEDIATE features (entropy_std) show moderate change; NEAR-STATIONARY features (entropy_max, entropy_min, tail_decay) remain approximately stable.

(c) Depth Classification via Leave-One-Generator-Out (LOGO):
The 8 generators are split into 7 training and 1 held-out test generator in a LOGO cross-validation scheme. An XGBoost classifier is trained on the 7 DDR features to predict generation depth class (gen-0 / gen-1 / gen-2+). This leak-free evaluation ensures the classifier generalizes across unseen generator architectures.
